# What an import read, and leaving rows out

Before an import is saved, it says which sheets and columns it read and which it did not, counts by sheet, and may leave named rows out with the rows that depend on them; worked-out cells a file edited are counted and said, never read.

## The rule

**What was read.** `readTables` knows each sheet by its header row. Besides the tables, it returns the sheets it read; the sheets it did not, each with why: `reading-only` (Results, Asks, Notes, a module's sheet such as Metrics), `not-faro` (a header row that is no Faro sheet's), `second` (a second sheet of one kind: only the first is read), `start-here` (the workbook's first sheet, or an older README, never a table and never mentioned); the **columns nothing reads** on each sheet it read (C19: named, never dropped silently); each table's headers as written; and the file's **origin**, the Start here sheet's "File of" row (the workspace's and cycle's ids). `readLine` says it in one sentence: "Read Goals. Not read: Results (for reading only); Budget (not a Faro sheet); the columns Notes and Budget on Goals. 2 example rows left out." Parts with nothing are left out.

**Another workspace's file** (`other-workspace`): when the origin's workspace isn't this one, it is asked before anything else, because the file's keys and IDs belong there. Answered "Add its rows as new goals", keys and IDs are dropped (and the Plan sheet, which needs keys) and the rows are read as new.

**Counts by sheet.** The change set counts unchanged rows by sheet (`unchangedBy`) beside its changes and issues, so the preview can give, per sheet read: rows read, added, changed, stopped or left, unchanged, rows to fix and rows to check.

**Leaving rows out** (decision 1: all or nothing unless the person chooses). `leaveOut(tables, rows)` returns the tables without those rows and without the rows that depend on them, each with why: a new goal's check-ins (named by its name, as a new goal has no key yet), goals whose Feeds into names it (and theirs in turn), and goals and Takes-over cells that name a new person left out.

**Worked-out cells.** `workedOutEdits` compares, for each row that matches a record by its key columns, the worked-out columns (Status, Now, Gap…) with what an export would write today. They are never read: a file that changes only them changes nothing, and the preview says so ("On 2 rows, Status differs from what Faro works out today. Faro never reads those columns: to change where a goal stands, post a check-in.").

## Worked examples

Each is run against the real rule by `src/spec/spec.test.ts`: the result is what the code gives.

| Given | The rule gives |
|---|---|
| A file with Start here, a Goals sheet with two columns of the person’s own (Notes, Budget), a Results sheet and a sheet called Budget. | `Read Goals. Not read: Results (for reading only); Budget (not a Faro sheet); the columns Notes and Budget on Goals.` |
| Leaving out Goals row 44 (a new goal) with 4 Check-ins rows for it and one goal (row 45) that feeds into it. | `5 rows go with it; row 45 because Feeds into names Goals row 44` |

## Not self-explanatory

- **Not self-explanatory:** The counts, the order of the blocks and the words of the preview are its screen's (spec/screens): a rebuild may lay them out its own way. Imported, Undo and Past imports come with IM4; paste and a header row below row 1 with IM5; large files with IM6.

## Requirements

- `IMPORT-PREVIEW`: Before anything is saved an import says which sheets and columns it read and which it did not, then counts by sheet, then what must be fixed, then its questions, then the changes on request with before and after and every default it used. Saving is all or nothing unless the person chooses to leave named rows out.

## Tests that check it

### [src/domain/importPreview.test.ts](../../../src/domain/importPreview.test.ts)

- rule 5: what was read › names the sheets read, those not read and why, and the columns nothing reads (C19)
- rule 5: what was read › a file with everything read says only what it read
- rule 8: leaving rows out › a new goal left out takes its check-ins and the goals that feed into it, each saying why
- rule 8: leaving rows out › a new person left out takes the goals they would own
- the counts by sheet › a row that changes nothing is counted on its own sheet
- the IM2 review, fixed in IM3 › an answer must be one the question offers: “banana” answers nothing
- the IM2 review, fixed in IM3 › one answer to an unlikely number covers only the numbers it was given for
- the IM2 review, fixed in IM3 › two rows answered “They’re the same” for one goal are named, not one dropped
- the IM2 review, fixed in IM3 › a near-miss goal name answered “Use …” is caught on two rows of one week
- the IM2 review, fixed in IM3 › a rename by key through MCP is a rename, and confirm answers the other-goal question
- the IM2 review, fixed in IM3 › “Leave these rows out” leaves out a non-admin’s Left row
- the IM2 review, fixed in IM3 › undoing an import that added a team removes the team again

### [src/domain/roundtrip.test.ts](../../../src/domain/roundtrip.test.ts)

- one format: export, load back, no change › ${d.name}: the workbook loads back as no change at all
- one format: export, load back, no change › ${d.name}: the zipped CSVs load back as no change at all
- the round trip is exact, whatever the day and the decimals › the demo as opened on ${day} loads back with no change
- the round trip is exact, whatever the day and the decimals › goals at 0, 1, 2 and 3 decimal places, in every plan shape, load back with no change
- one format: an edited copy applies exactly its edits › through the workbook
- one format: an edited copy applies exactly its edits › through the zipped CSVs, with the formula guard taken off again
- a typed cell is the same as what was written › compares numbers at the column’s written precision, never with a tolerance
- one reader › reads RFC 4180 CSV in one pass: quotes, doubled quotes, line breaks in a cell, a byte-order mark, CRLF
- one reader › knows each sheet by its header, whatever the file is called
- a module’s own sheet in a file loaded back (AS part 3) › is named as written for reading, not called unknown
- worked-out cells a file edited (rule 9, C19) › an unedited workbook has none; Status edited on two rows is named, and still changes nothing
